key_insight: Specialized, physics-aware machine learning force fields are needed to accurately model complex materials dynamics where general-purpose ML potentials break down on reactive, non-equilibrium, or nonlocal phenomena.
engineering_relevance: For atomistic simulation workflows, the review argues that task-specific MLIPs can enable reliable prediction of interfaces, open systems, phase evolution, and fracture while preserving computational efficiency.
method: Benchmark MLIPs against the target observable, not just near-equilibrium accuracy.
Adapt model architecture and training data to capture strained, reactive, and nonlocal configurations.
Balance accuracy, scaling cost, and physical consistency when selecting universal versus specialized force fields.
evidence_signal: The review compares specialized MLIP needs across four demanding application contexts: electrified interfaces, compositionally fluctuating open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture.
watch_item: High-order message passing and overly broad models can be computationally expensive and may still fail on out-of-distribution reactive states if not validated for the intended use case.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
